question: In which year did the Supreme Court give its judgement in the 'Satbir Singh versus the State of Haryana' case, which was related to dowry issues?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court delivered its judgement in the 'Satbir Singh versus the State of Haryana' case in **2021**.
 
• The case primarily dealt with the issue of **dowry harassment** and cruelty under Section 304B (Dowry Death) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
 
• The judgement emphasized that **mental cruelty** related to dowry demands can be a significant factor in dowry death cases.
 
• The court clarified the interpretation of Section 304B IPC, focusing on the phrase "**soon before her death**," asserting that it must be understood in proximity to the cruelty or harassment faced by the victim.
 
• This ruling was a landmark in strengthening legal measures against dowry-related crimes and ensuring justice for victims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961:**

 
 
• This law prohibits the giving or taking of dowry in India.
 
• Dowry is defined as any property or valuable security given directly or indirectly in connection with marriage.
 
• The Act aims to curb the social evil of dowry, which has been a major contributor to cruelty and violence against women.
 
 
 
• **Section 304B IPC (Dowry Death):**
 
 
• This section provides punishment for dowry-related deaths of women.
 
• If a woman's death occurs under suspicious circumstances within 7 years of marriage, and she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry, it is considered a dowry death.
 
• The punishment for the accused is imprisonment for a term not less than 7 years, which may extend to life imprisonment.
 
 
 
• **Section 498A IPC:**
 
 
• This section deals with cruelty by a husband or his relatives towards a married woman.
 
• Cruelty includes physical or mental harm, harassment for dowry, and driving the woman to suicide or grave injury.
 
• It is a cognizable and non-bailable offense.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Judgements like Satbir Singh Case:**
 
 
• They help strengthen the legal framework to protect women from dowry-related abuses.
 
• Such rulings provide clarity on the interpretation of legal provisions, ensuring better enforcement of laws.
 
• They highlight the seriousness of the dowry problem and the urgent need for social reform.
